title: DIY Intervention Planner
intro: For families who can stay united and execute the basics. This planner prepares one meeting around the care the person needs. TAP remains the source of truth for placement and logistics.
privacy: Private to this account · Protected on this device
safetyTitle: Safety and voluntary help override every plan
safetyBody: Call 911 for overdose or immediate danger. Call or text 988 for a mental-health crisis. If they ask for treatment now, act now—do not delay help to finish this planner.
helpNow: They're asking for treatment now — open immediate help
loadErrorTitle: Protected planner could not be opened
loadErrorBody: Editing is blocked so unknown protected data cannot be overwritten.
startOver: Clear protected planner and start over
clearBody: This permanently removes this account's protected DIY plan from this device. TAP is not cleared.
saveError: The latest change is not safely stored.
readyBody: The team has one clinically indicated solution, TAP logistics are saved, the bed matches the date, and the meeting, Planned No, and AMA response are prepared.
notReadyTitle: Not ready to hold the intervention
notReadyBody: Finish each open gate in order. A divided team, missing bed, lower level of care, unsaved TAP, or incomplete chapter keeps the intervention blocked.
locked: Complete the prior stage before opening this chapter.
professionalNote: If the family cannot unite or needs step-by-step execution coaching, stop DIY. A professional intervention is the safer off-ramp—not another app lesson.

stages.program: 3. Program, contact, and bed — in TAP

fit.body: Answer for the situation as it is today. Any safety stop ends DIY planning.
fit.childrenCannotExit: Children who cannot be safely gotten out of the house?
fit.familyUnitedOnOneSolution: Can the family agree on one solution?
fit.canExecuteBasicsWithoutTutorial: Can the family execute basic logistics without a step-by-step tutorial?
fit.emergencyTitle: Stop DIY and use immediate safety help
fit.emergencyBody: Do not continue into letters or rehearsal. Use 911 or 988 as appropriate and involve a qualified professional.
fit.professionalTitle: DIY is not the right fit
fit.professionalBody: Do not proceed with a divided team or a plan that requires detailed staging. Talk with a professional interventionist.

care.body: Choose the level indicated by the situation—not the lower level the person may accept.

education.detox: Detox: medical management when withdrawal may be dangerous or needs monitoring.
education.residential: Residential: 24-hour structure when safety and stability cannot hold outside treatment.
education.php: PHP: intensive daytime treatment with a safe, stable place outside program hours.
education.iop: IOP: multiple treatment sessions weekly when the person can remain safe between sessions.
education.outpatient: Outpatient: lower-frequency care when risk and instability do not require more structure.

care.why: Why this level—in the family's words
care.temptation: Optional: lower level they say they might accept
care.temptationNote: This records the temptation. It does not become the plan.
care.plan: Level of care in the actual plan
care.gap: The planned level does not match the indicated need. This stage cannot turn ready.

program.body: TAP owns program, contact, confirmed bed, coverage, transport, bag, documents, money, and backup. This planner reads those facts and does not duplicate them.
program.missing: TAP is not yet saved and ready for this intervention date.
program.finderNote: The A–Z finder is a directory only. Listings are not rankings, sponsorships, clinical recommendations, or guarantees. Confirm directly with the program.

team.body: List the people involved and assign one role. No active use, competing solution, or child in the room.
team.name: Name
team.aligned: Aligned with the one solution and TAP leave time?
team.undercutter: Who is most likely to say they do not need to go today?
team.undercutterAgrees: Does this person agree to the one solution and leave time?
team.undercutterBlocked: If they do not agree, they cannot be a speaker or silent support in the room.

unity.body: One indicated level, one program, one date, one leave time, one bed. Every involved team member aligns or the meeting stays blocked.
unity.solutionConfirmed: I confirm this is the team's one solution
unity.yesPlaceholder: Use the program and leave time already confirmed in TAP.
unity.plannedNo: Planned No: money and housing consequences already agreed
unity.noDebate: A Planned No is not an argument or collapse. Start the written consequences that day and end the conversation.

letters.body: Each speaker writes their own short letter. The app provides an outline, not invented life history.
letters.facts: Specific recent facts—not a lifetime prosecution
letters.request: The request: this program and this time
letters.boundary: My own boundary if the answer is no
letters.complete: Speaker confirms this letter is complete
letters.rules: No diagnosis, humiliation, invented details, or extra ultimatums outside the team's Planned No.

rehearsal.body: Rehearse the meeting: speaking order, one facilitator, one person holding the floor, one ask, and a clean move to Yes or Planned No.
rehearsal.debateHolder: Who holds the floor when debate starts
rehearsal.stopDebate: Stop debate and return to the request
rehearsal.noStacking: Read letters without stacking on or humiliating
rehearsal.needsStaging: We need detailed physical staging or execution coaching
rehearsal.needsStagingNote: Stop DIY and use the professional off-ramp.

execute.body: Prepare the day-of run sheet and the AMA response. This chapter does not replace TAP logistics.
execute.familyNotRide: Family is not the ride home
execute.tapBackup: Then use the TAP backup path
execute.dayLocked: Day-of controls unlock only after stages 1–7 and TAP are ready.
execute.yesOutcome: Yes—left for the program with the bed
